summary: Iter 228y — Verified slot-locked team invite tokens (NEW backend + frontend) + glowing-horn regression for draft picks on the trade block. 25/25 backend tests green (10 new iter228y + 3 iter228w bullhorn + 12 trade_block_router regression). Live smoke tests against the deployed API confirmed all 5 new endpoints behave per spec, including 403 for non-commissioner mint, single-use token, email-lock enforcement, and `current_teams` bump on accept. Frontend /team-invites/:token claim page renders both the 'Invite unavailable' state (invalid token) and the valid 'Pending — claim it / Sign in / Claim Team' state. /commissioner/owner-invites shows the new Slot invites column with: Mint open link (no email), Mint locked link (auto-appears when an email is typed into the row's input), 'Add co-owner' on the already-owned team (Zarek's Frozen / chriszarek), Owner chips with copy + X revoke controls, 'Slot invite created' toast on success, and the pre-existing 'Invite All' bulk flow still rendered. /team Roster page has the section header block toggles (data-testid roster-draft-section-block-toggle-* — 2 sections detected) and animate-pulse glow classes wired. No critical bugs found.

minor.issue: Response still leaks Mongo `_id` (ObjectId). Pre-existing, not introduced by iter228y — flagged for future cleanup.

action_items: (Optional) Exclude `_id` from GET /api/trade-block responses for consistency with rest of API.
(Optional) Confirmation prompt before destructive 'Revoke' (X) chip click — currently revokes immediately without a confirm dialog. Low priority UX nit.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/team_invites.py L116-119: `_invite_status` correctly handles naive expires_at by treating as UTC — good defensive coding for older docs.

routes/team_invites.py L286-298: `current_teams` bump uses an `$inc` guarded by `if not team.get('owner_id')` BEFORE the team is updated — correct logic (the old document is checked, not the post-update state). No race condition because the same handler holds the request scope.
routes/team_invites.py L283-285: Promoting a co-owner to owner strips them from co_owner_ids — good edge case handling.
routes/team_invites.py L48-52: `_frontend_base` falls back to a hard-coded preview URL when FRONTEND_URL env var is missing. Acceptable safety net but consider raising in prod.

test_iter228y_team_invites.py: 10 well-scoped pytest cases covering all major branches (happy-path, email lock, single-use, co-owner add/double, owner-already-owned, revoke, expired, listing filter, non-commissioner 403). Great coverage.
